title: Seller's Property Disclosure Report
description: Vermont requires sellers of residential real property to complete a property condition disclosure report. While Vermont does not have a single comprehensive mandatory disclosure statute like many states, standard practice and Vermont Real Estate Commission rules require disclosure of known material defects. The Vermont Association of Realtors provides a standard disclosure form that has become the industry norm.

required_actions.note: Vermont relies on common law duty and industry practice. Standard disclosure form should be provided before binding contract.

title: Lead Paint Disclosure and Essential Maintenance Practices
description: Vermont has among the strongest lead paint laws in the nation. Under 18 V.S.A. §1759 et seq., sellers and landlords must disclose known lead paint hazards. Vermont's Essential Maintenance Practices (EMP) law requires property owners to maintain pre-1978 housing using lead-safe practices and to file an EMP compliance statement. Vermont ELHD (Elevated Lead in Housing Database) tracking adds an additional enforcement layer beyond federal requirements.

required_actions.note: Vermont requires Essential Maintenance Practices (EMP) filing. EMP compliance is verified by the state. Penalties for non-compliance are substantial.

title: Agency Disclosure and Consent
description: Vermont requires written disclosure of brokerage relationships before any substantive contact. Dual agency requires written informed consent from both parties. Vermont Real Estate Commission rules mandate clear disclosure of whether the licensee represents the buyer, seller, both, or neither.

required_actions.note: Must be provided at first substantive contact. Dual agency consent must be documented and signed by both parties.

title: Closing Practice — Attorney Commonly Used
description: Vermont is not technically an attorney-only close state by statute, but attorneys are very commonly involved in closings. Vermont practice strongly favors attorney involvement for title examination, deed preparation, and closing supervision. Many lenders require attorney involvement for Vermont transactions.

required_actions.note: Attorney involvement strongly recommended and common practice. Many lenders require it.

title: Well and Septic/Wastewater System Disclosure
description: Vermont requires disclosure of water supply and wastewater system information. Under 10 V.S.A. §1978, sellers must disclose the type and condition of water supply (well, spring, community) and wastewater disposal (septic, municipal sewer). Vermont's Water Supply Rule and Wastewater System and Potable Water Supply Rules add regulatory requirements for private systems.

required_actions.note: Disclose water supply type, well condition, septic system type, age, and last pump-out date.

citations: Vermont Wastewater System and Potable Water Supply Rules (Env. DEC Ch. 1)

title: Act 250 Land Use Permit Disclosure
description: Vermont's Act 250 (10 V.S.A. Chapter 151) requires a land use permit for developments meeting certain thresholds. Sellers must disclose any existing Act 250 permits and conditions that bind the property, as these run with the land and are enforceable against subsequent owners.

required_actions.note: All Act 250 permit conditions run with the land. Buyer must be informed of all active conditions and compliance obligations.
